transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (Redwood CSM), Jenna Maxwell (CTO, Northbridge), Ibrahim Khan (Lead ML Eng), Sasha Park (Infra Manager), Liam O'Connor (PM)

Summary (auto): Northbridge is near decision point for moving some production inference from hosted vendors into a private/Dedicated setup. Priority: production latency 90th p99 targets, strict EU data residency, and SDK compatibility with LangChain/LlamaIndex flows currently running in-house. They asked about gateway-proxy architectures, quota enforcement, observability hooks (traces, per-route token cost), and keys/KMS/HSM integration.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sophie from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with me is mateo ruiz our solutions engineer, and ava from CSM, how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jenna: good, thanks, busy week but glad we could make time.
[00:08] Ibrahim: morning all, thanks for coordinating. Sorry if i sound a bit echoey, i'm on a headset.
[00:12] Mateo: no worries, we can hear you fine. quick agenda: we want to understand your current stack, expected QPS and latency SLOS, any compliance constraints, and then map those to hosted / dedicated / private migration options and a potential POC. sound ok?
[00:22] Liam: yep that's perfect. we also want to see what the integration effort looks like given we've built a lot of orchestration around langchain and a LlamaIndex style index layer.
[00:30] Sophie: great, could you give us a quick picture of current traffic and what you're trying to achieve?
[00:35] Jenna: sure. at a top level we have two production services: a customer support assistant that does 2–3 rps average but spikes to ~120 rps during business hours; and an analytics summary pipeline that runs batch embeddings and retriever calls, about 40 qps during nightly windows. target latency for the support assistant is p90 < 250ms for short prompts, p99 < 600ms ideally.
[00:53] Ibrahim: and importantly, the company policy is EU residency for all logs and user data. we're an EU-registered entity so any hosted vendor must either have EU regions or we need a private deployment.
[01:05] Sophie: understood. so you're evaluating whether to stay hosted and pick region-based hosting, reserve Dedicated pools for throughput predictability, or do private (VPC/on-prem). a couple quick questions: do you need model ownership or are you open to Redwood curated open models?
[01:18] Jenna: we don't need to own models, but we need predictable performance and the ability to run on-prem later if compliance demands it. cost is a concern but latency and compliance are higher priority.
[01:28] Mateo: sounds typical. given the spikes you described, Dedicated with burst or a Private VPC makes sense — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so you get throughput SLOs, private gives you full control for residency and KMS integration. you mentioned langchain and llamaindex — can you say how those are wired in?
[01:44] Liam: we have a microservice 'retriever' that uses LlamaIndex to build dense indices, and a separate convo orchestrator that wraps LangChain chains with a proxy for routing calls to different models/environments. it's all in python.
[01:58] Ibrahim: right now we call OpenAI for hosted, but we have a gateway proxy layer that injects metadata, enforces per-user quotas and manipulates prompts for persona routing. we're looking for a seamless drop-in for the model endpoint and ideally sdk helpers for langchain/llamaindex.
[02:15] Mateo: okay, good. Redwood's SDKs are python-first, we have an official LangChain integration adapter and a connector example for LlamaIndex. i'll follow up with code snippets after the call. small caveat — some of the adapter names in our docs are auto-terranscribed as 'red wood adapter' in older assets, but the package is redwood-inference-sdk on pip.
[02:33] Jenna: haha okay noted. can you talk about the gateway/proxy pattern — we want to keep our enrichments and routing in place. is it possible to keep that and still get batching and kv cache benefits?
[02:44] Mateo: yes, there are two common patterns. 1) keep your edge gateway and proxy the requests to Redwood's hosted endpoints — in this case Redwood's smart-routing and batching is applied on our side; prefix caching is limited because we see requests post-proxy, but KV cache can be enabled via session tokens. 2) deploy a lightweight sidecar or on-prem proxy that speaks to your gateway internally and then forwards to Redwood — the sidecar can manage request coalescing and attach cache keys so the Redwood runtime can do prefix/K V cache hits. the sidecar approach is recommended for private deployment to preserve caching.
[03:18] Sasha: sidecar sounds interesting. we have tight change control though, so low-lift options are preferred. any out-of-the-box tooling for rate-limits and quotas at the route level? we currently enforce quotas in the gateway and want to keep per-customer spend caps.
[03:32] Sophie: Redwood supports per-token quotas and per-route rate limits in the Console — you can set quotas per API key and per route, and we expose telemetry to show token consumption. for Dedicated, quotas are enforced at your tenant boundary; for Private, you can plug into your existing RBAC. we also expose webhook alerts when a quota threshold is reached.
[03:51] Ibrahim: who owns rate limiting vs us? like, if we set per-user caps in our gateway and then a second layer in Redwood, how do they interact?
[03:59] Mateo: they stack. your gateway's check happens first; if the gateway allows, Redwood will enforce the configured quota. we recommend doing coarse gating in your gateway (e.g., per-session) and fine-grained cost controls inside Redwood. that dual-layer prevents accidental spikes.
[04:14] Liam: can we get per-route token cost breakdowns in traces? we need to map features to cost for product analytics.
[04:21] Sophie: yes — Console and the telemetry API provide token level attribution per request id, model, and route. you can stream traces into your observability (we have native exporters for Datadog, New Relic, and OpenTelemetry). Mateo, did you want to add on the observability hooks?
[04:33] Mateo: sure. we surface per-request metrics (latency, tokens_in/out, model version), spans for request lifecycle, and logs for model fallback events. you can attach custom tags in the SDK which show up in traces. also there's an eval hooks endpoint to report prompt-level QA metrics back to Redwood Optimize for regression alerts.
[04:55] Jenna: about fallbacks — if a model variant is slow or down, will Redwood automatically route to another variant? and can we control that fallback policy?
[05:03] Mateo: yes, smart-routing supports automated fallback to model variants or to a lower-cost tier. you can configure policy: prefer-latency, cost-first, or strict pin (no fallback). in Dedicated we have stricter controls for pinning model versions.
[05:18] Ibrahim: ok that helps. on security: we need SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS for encrypting audio / prompt logs. also HSM options for some keys. do you provide HSM integration?
[05:30] Sophie: we integrate with cloud KMS providers and offer HSM via private deployment engagements. for Hosted we provide envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in supported regions; for Private you can bring your own HSM or use an enterprise HSM appliance. we'll share the SOC 2 / ISO artifacts.
[05:45] Ava: and just to add, our enterprise package includes audit log retention options and optional dedicated log streams to your SIEM.
[05:52] Sasha: good. one more compliance Q: since we're EU registered, can you guarantee logs don't leave EU?
[05:58] Mateo: for Hosted, yes if you select our EU region. for Dedicated, we provision capacity in EU and keep telemetry there. for Private, everything stays inside your VPC/on-prem. we do recommend explicit contractual language for data residency — we can add that to the pilot SOW.
[06:13] Liam: back to integration: how much change in our LangChain chains? we use a custom PromptTemplate and a small shim around the LLM call. ideally we swap out the client and keep the rest intact.
[06:25] Mateo: that's the usual pattern. the SDK exposes a LangChain LLM wrapper class that implements the standard llm interface. for LlamaIndex we have a connector that accepts index queries directly; code-wise it's typically a few lines: instantiate Red woodClient, wrap with LangChain LLM, feed into the chain. i'll send example gist.
[06:40] Ibrahim: is streaming supported? we rely on partial generation for the UI to show incremental responses.
[06:44] Sophie: yes, streaming supported in Hosted and Dedicated. Private supports streaming too but requires configuring the sidecar/proxy to support chunked responses. small note: streaming semantics differ by model family, but our SDK normalizes them.
[06:58] Jenna: about benchmarking — we want to do a small latency benchmark comparing current hosted vendor, Redwood Hosted EU region, and a Dedicated pool. what sample payloads should we provide?
[07:08] Mateo: send us representative prompts (short + long), context window sizes, and average token lengths; ideally two API endpoints you currently hit for the conversational and retrieval flows. we will run steady-state and spike tests, and provide p50/p90/p99 numbers with token cost estimates.
[07:23] Liam: how long does a Dedicated provisioning take? if we sign pilot, when could we get a Dedicated pool?
[07:29] Sophie: Dedicated can be provisioned in ~2 weeks for standard configs; if you need special hardware or EU-specific procurement it can be 3–4 weeks. Private on-prem typically runs longer — depends on network/install windows.
[07:40] Ibrahim: any limits around quota throttles during spiky traffic? we can't drop requests at the gateway because we need guaranteed responses for certain SLAs.
[07:49] Mateo: we offer autoscaling and burst capacity for Dedicated which helps absorb spikes; policy can be configured to queue or to fail fast. for strict SLAs, Dedicated with reserved capacity and burst buffer is the best fit.
[07:59] Jenna: question on caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier. how transparent is that? we rely on session-level memory for followup queries.
[08:07] Mateo: KV cache is exposed as a session feature — you can use session tokens and produce cache keys from your sidecar. for Hosted without sidecar, prefix caching is limited because we don't see your pre-proxy context; for Private sidecar patterns you get near-native KV cache benefits.
[08:23] Sophie: quick clarification — when we say Private we mean a customer-managed control plane that can run in VPC or on-prem with Redwood's runtime inside your network. many customers start Hosted, then Dedicated, then move a fraction to Private for regulatory workloads.
[08:36] Liam: sounds like our path could be: start with Dedicated EU region for predictability, run a pilot for 6 weeks, then migrate a subset to Private for EU-only logs.
[08:45] Sasha: yep that maps to what compliance asked for. what's the billing model for Dedicated and Private? flat capacity fees + per-token?
[08:53] Sophie: Dedicated is monthly reserved GPU capacity + per-token usage for generation and embeddings; there are options for commit levels to reduce unit cost. Private has a platform fee + support tier and can be either usage-based or flat depending on the contract. for burst usage, we have an overage rate or configurable burst buckets.
[09:09] Ibrahim: any limitations on model quantization or custom quant profiles in Private? we have some latency-sensitive models where quantization is important.
[09:17] Mateo: in Private you can apply custom quantization profiles and kernel selection policies; for Dedicated we support a set of vetted quant profiles that are tested on the runtime — we can onboard custom profiles as part of an eng engagement.
[09:31] Jenna: about log redaction — we need PII redaction on stored prompts. is that done client-side or do you provide tools?
[09:38] Ava: we surface redaction hooks and an SDK helper that can run a pre-send scrubber. many customers run client-side redaction plus server-side rules. we'll include the redaction guidance doc in the pack.
[09:50] Liam: i want to double-check the LangChain adapter — does it handle function-calling or only simple completions?
[09:57] Mateo: our LangChain adapter supports streaming, function-calling and structured output. function-calls map to a 'tools' pattern in LangChain — we provide examples for both python and node.
[10:08] Ibrahim: latency-wise, will we see different p99s for function calling flows? we use a lot of tool-calls that add extra round trips.
[10:15] Mateo: function calling can add overhead depending on your orchestration and any external tool latencies; Redwood's runtime minimizes overhead for the model call itself but the orchestration layer's network hops still count. for best p99 you want to collocate your orchestration layer or use a sidecar to reduce extra network hops.
[10:32] Jenna: ok good. any gotchas for our retriever + LlamaIndex flow? our retriever does dense vector queries to an in-house vector DB and then we pass top K contexts to the LLM.
[10:42] Mateo: that's common. two suggestions: 1) use embedding batching to reduce token costs in batch jobs, 2) when building the prompt include only top K contexts and let Redwood's per-request token accounting show cost. if you want tighter caching for retrieval results, consider caching embedding vectors on your sidecar and set TTLs.
[10:59] Sasha: are there any SDK rate-limit defaults we should be aware of? we've experienced 429s from other vendors during spikes.
[11:06] Sophie: SDKs have client-side retry/backoff with jitter. server-side rate limits vary by plan; during a spike, Dedicated reserved capacity reduces the chance of 429 because you have allocated GPUs. we also offer exponential backoff policies and token-level budgeting.
[11:20] Liam: fine. how do we instrument cost attribution in our product analytics? can we send request ids mapping to user ids without leaking PII?
[11:28] Mateo: yes — you can attach non-PII custom tags (e.g., account_id_hash) that appear in telemetry. we recommend hashing or tokenizing PII before tagging. Console exposes per-route cost breakdown and you can export per-request CSVs via the telemetry API.
[11:42] Jenna: about SSO, can we integrate Redwood Console with our SAML provider and do SCIM provisioning?
[11:47] Sophie: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user accounts. for Dedicated and Private we can also offer integrations with your existing IdP and RBAC sync.
[11:58] Ibrahim: security folks will want to see pentest reports and the SOC documentation. can we get those?
[12:02] Ava: yes, we'll share SOC2 report, pen test summary, and the data flow diagram. we'll obfuscate any sensitive vendor details as needed.
[12:11] Liam: what's the POC timeline? we want to run a 4–6 week pilot, focus on support assistant and embedding nightly job.
[12:17] Sophie: that's doable. POC typically: week 0 onboarding + credentials and region setup, week 1–2 integration + smoke tests, week 3 run bench workloads, week 4 iterate and tune for latency/cost. then wrap with results and an ops runbook.
[12:31] Ibrahim: and what do you need from us to start?
[12:33] Mateo: sample prompts (short/long), two endpoints to benchmark, expected concurrency patterns, any model preferences (family, sequence length), and contact for infra to enable VPC peering if needed.
[12:46] Jenna: we'll prepare that. also we want to see a sample SLA for Dedicated and an example SOW for private deployment.
[12:52] Sophie: will do. i'll include SLA language and a draft SOW for Private.
[12:57] Liam: one small question — cost controls: can we set hard-spend caps that stop calls if exceeded?
[13:03] Mateo: yes, you can set hard caps that cause calls to fail fast, and soft caps that emit alerts. we recommend soft + webhook alerting for production but hard-caps for dev/test.
[13:14] Sasha: ok that's helpful. any remaining integration risks you foresee?
[13:19] Mateo: main ones are: network topology for low-latency (collocate sidecar), differences in streaming semantics (we provide normalization), and ensuring your gateway preserves necessary metadata for quotas and caching. none are blockers — all are engineering workstreams we can support.
[13:35] Sophie: great. quick recap and next steps: we'll share Dedicated pricing and pilot contract, Mateo will send LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK examples and a gateway sidecar pattern repo, Ava will push SOC2 and security pack, and Northbridge will provide sample prompts and endpoints to benchmark.
[13:53] Jenna: sounds good. can you timebox the next technical kickoff to 30–45 minutes next week?
[13:58] Sophie: yes, we'll propose times in the follow-up. thanks everyone.
[14:03] Ibrahim: thanks, talk soon.

Notes / misc: occasional transcription glitches - 'K V cash' heard instead of 'KV cache' in a couple places; package name transcribed as 'red wood' in one spot. References to shared artifacts: 'Dedicated pricing deck', 'security pack (SOC2, pen test summary)', 'LangChain and LlamaIndex sample repo', 'benchmark results spreadsheet'.

End of transcript.
